questions.question: A researcher wants to study the impact of divorce on children. Evaluate which method would be most appropriate.

points.text: Semi-structured interviews: allow children to express experiences, follow up on sensitive topics, build rapport. Ethical issues: consent from parents AND children, protection from distress.

questions.question: Compare the practical and ethical issues of researching crime vs education.

points.text: Crime: greater ethical issues (risk, illegal activity, deception). Education: access challenges (gatekeepers, parental consent). Both require sensitivity but crime faces greater ethical dilemmas.

questions.question: Evaluate whether triangulation always produces better research than a single method.

points.text: Triangulation strengths: overcomes individual method limitations, increases validity, provides complete picture. Weaknesses: more time/cost, may produce contradictory findings. Conclusion: generally preferable but not always practical.
